decisions.mark: distinguishes the two ways to substitute an allocator — a COMPILE-time pair of macros versus a RUNTIME pair of function pointers — and states that they are mutually exclusive
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "Compile-time macros. Enable `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY` and define both `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO`... The runtime setter is not compiled in at all in this mode, so calling it fails to link." and "(no runtime pointers, and platform.c:20-64 is compiled out)" | WHY: The answer separates the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer setter and states that macros compile out the runtime pointers and setter, which means the two are mutually exclusive. || QUOTE: "Compile-time macros. Enable `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY` and define both `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO`... The runtime setter is not compiled in at all in this mode, so calling it fails to link." | WHY: The answer separates the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer pair, and it says the runtime setter is compiled out when the macros are defined ("no runtime pointers, and platform.c:20-64 is compiled out"), which is mutual exclusivity. || QUOTE: "Compile-time macros. Enable `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_MEMORY` and define both `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_CALLOC_MACRO` and `MBEDTLS_PLATFORM_FREE_MACRO`... The runtime setter is not compiled in at all in this mode, so calling it fails to link." and "(no runtime pointers, and platform.c:20-64 is compiled out)" | WHY: The answer distinguishes the compile-time macro pair from the runtime function-pointer setter. It says the macros compile out the runtime pointers and setter, so the two are mutually exclusive.
